title: Draft Stacks, No Classes, Composite Type, Ray Faces & Self-Styling Data
description: A film synced to its rough drafts, a page with no classes, four fonts as one family, faces built from rays, and CSV that styles itself.

drops.title: The Draft Underneath
drops.description: A finished motion piece and the four rough blockouts it grew from, all driven by one clock.
drops.concept: Null Motion plays an ad on top of the drafts it came from and exports the lot as a breakdown. This rebuilds the playback half: one timeline, five renderers, with the draft whose section is on screen following frame for frame while the other three loop their own beat. Scrub, slow down, or fade the blockout back over the finish.
drops.source: blixvip/NullMotion — play a finished motion-graphics ad in sync with its rough drafts

interaction.mouse: Drag the scrubber to move every renderer at once; speed and ghost sliders in the panel.
interaction.click: Pause to inspect a single frame, or switch the idle drafts between looping and held.
interaction.touch: Scrubber, transport and panel are all touch targets; the draft strip reflows to two columns.

drops.title: A Page With No Classes
drops.description: The same class-free document rendered bare, under a classless sheet, and under your own tokens.
drops.concept: Sumi.css styles plain semantic HTML and wraps every rule in :where(), so the framework carries no specificity at all. Three shadow roots hold identical markup — nothing has a class attribute — and a plain h2 rule added on top wins the cascade without !important. The tokens drive an auto-fit grid, a fluid type scale and a dark theme on the host.
drops.source: vladocar/Sumi.css — a minimalist, classless-first CSS framework

interaction.mouse: Token sliders retune the third pane live: grid minimum, type ratio, radius, density, accent hue.
interaction.click: Flip the theme, or add the plain h2 rule and watch zero-specificity rules give way.
interaction.touch: Panes stack on narrow screens; each one scrolls on its own.

drops.title: One Typeface, Four Fonts
drops.description: A composite family assembled live from four faces, split by unicode-range and tuned per slice.
drops.concept: InDesign has composite fonts: one logical typeface whose Latin, figures, marks and CJK each come from a different font, sized and aligned to sit together. CSS can do most of it — the same font-family name declared four times, each with its own unicode-range and size-adjust. The sliders rewrite the face set, and a canvas measurement shows the digit run actually changing width inside an unchanged text node.
drops.source: charlie5188/css-composite-font — InDesign-style composite fonts for CJK and Western text

interaction.mouse: Four sliders retune the figures, marks and CJK slices and regenerate the @font-face block.
interaction.click: Cycle three recipes, or switch the composite off to see one family doing all four jobs.
interaction.touch: Specimen and generated CSS stack and scroll; the tuning panel hides on small screens.

drops.title: A Face Built From Rays
drops.description: Outlines sampled as 128 radii, springs at 120 Hz, and pupils rotated on a sphere toward your cursor.
drops.concept: A reverse-engineering of the GrokBot avatar engine: no pre-rendered frames, shape changes by interpolating a radial outline ray by ray, motion by semi-implicit Euler springs rather than timers, and pseudo-3D eyes made by rotating a point on a sphere with Rodrigues' formula and projecting it flat. Only changed attributes are written back to the SVG, and the loop parks itself when the springs settle.
drops.source: ArvinYin1/grokbot-animation-anatomy — reverse-engineered anatomy of the GrokBot avatar engine

interaction.mouse: Every face leans and looks toward the pointer; hovering one morphs its outline to the next shape.
interaction.click: Click a face to blink it on demand; toggle flat pupils or show the rays the outline is built from.
interaction.touch: Tap a face to blink and morph it; the rig panel is desktop-only.

drops.title: The File That Styles Itself
drops.description: CSV with a CSS block on top, rendered into a shadow root that asks the stylesheet which column is the key.
drops.concept: CSSV puts a stylesheet between two --- rules at the top of a CSV file, so a data export arrives already dressed. The element parses the document, detects the delimiter and the numeric columns, renders the table inside a shadow root so nothing leaks, then reads --cssv-key back out of the computed style to decide which column becomes each row's data-key. Break the file and it renders nothing and fires cssv-error with fatal: true.
drops.source: rhpaiva/cssv — CSV data with a CSS stylesheet at the top of the same file

interaction.mouse: Edit the file and the table re-renders as you type; three sample documents to switch between.
interaction.click: Toggle a shared imported sheet, numeric alignment or zebra rows — then corrupt the file on purpose.
interaction.touch: Editor and render stack vertically; the sample file pills stay tappable.
